holidays.name: International Skeptics Day
holidays.description: A day for questioning everything, demanding evidence, and raising an eyebrow at claims that sound too good to be true. Celebrants are encouraged to think critically, and to doubt this very description.
holidays.origin: Observed in connection with Skeptics Day, promoted by skeptic and critical-thinking communities as a day to champion science and evidence-based reasoning.
holidays.funFact: The day is sometimes tied to Friday the 13th superstitions, which skeptics love to debunk, since there's no good evidence that the date brings bad luck.

holidays.name: National Yorkshire Pudding Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the puffy, golden, crispy-edged British baked batter traditionally served with roast beef and gravy. Bonus points if yours rises higher than your expectations.
holidays.origin: Observed in the UK and by food lovers elsewhere, usually on the first Sunday of February, though some food calendars also list it in autumn.
holidays.funFact: Yorkshire puddings were originally called 'dripping puddings' because the batter was cooked under roasting meat to catch the drippings.

holidays.name: National No Bra Day
holidays.description: An awareness day that began as a way to encourage breast cancer awareness and early screening. It has since become widely known on social media.
holidays.origin: Created in 2011 as a social media awareness campaign and observed on October 13 each year in the United States.
holidays.funFact: The day falls during Breast Cancer Awareness Month, and many organizations use it to promote self-exams and mammogram reminders.

holidays.name: Train Your Brain Day
holidays.description: A day for mental workouts such as puzzles, crosswords, learning a new skill, or finally figuring out how to fold a fitted sheet. Your brain gets a gym membership for 24 hours.
holidays.origin: An unofficial observance created by brain-fitness enthusiasts to encourage lifelong learning and mental stimulation.
holidays.funFact: Neuroscientists call the brain's ability to rewire itself 'neuroplasticity,' and it continues throughout adulthood, so you really can teach an old dog new tricks.

holidays.name: Navy Birthday
holidays.description: A day when the United States Navy celebrates its founding with ceremonies, cake, and plenty of nautical pride. Sailors everywhere get a good excuse for a party.
holidays.origin: The Continental Congress authorized the first naval force on October 13, 1775, creating what became the U.S. Navy.
holidays.funFact: The first Continental Navy ships were converted merchant vessels, so the Navy began life essentially as a fleet of repurposed cargo boats.
